# Continual-ARC pattern note

For the task demonstrated here, sparse diagonal clues encode a repeating diagonal-periodic color tile. The output is filled across the entire grid with rows shifted cyclically by one cell each row (colors constant on diagonals of slope +1, i.e. constant `c-r mod k`). Infer the cycle length and color order from clue colors/positions, then repeat across the given dimensions.

Evidence: 28x28 demo output repeats four colors with rows shifted: row0 `9,5,8,3,...`, row1 `3,9,5,8,...`, hence value depends on `(c-r) mod 4`, with residues mapped `0→9, 1→5, 2→8, 3→3`. For the 15x15 test, accepted output had row0 `4,2,1,...`, row1 `2,1,4,...`, so period 3 and mapping `(c-r) mod 3`: residue 0→4, 1→2, 2→1. A first guess using [1,2,4] and a reverse cycle failed; use clue placements to derive the residue-to-color mapping carefully.

# Continual-ARC task notes (task-4cd0f038)

This instance ended unsolved after 8 submissions and 6 demo requests. Do not treat any submitted output as verified. Useful observed pattern across demos: background color stays unchanged; pairs of same-color cells on a diagonal act as a directional line seed, and the line is extended in the diagonal direction indicated by the pair, often to the grid edge. Those guesses were wrong. One demo pair may show distinct directions for different colors, so establish each ray's direction from local seed arrangement. This note is a heuristic only, not a confirmed complete rule.

# Continual-ARC observed pattern

## Divider panels: propagate a filled tile into blank panels

Evidence: task-3430aeff, demo 1 and solved test.

When a grid uses color 6 as full-width horizontal separators and a full-height vertical divider, these delimit equal-sized panels. A panel containing a colored pattern can be the source; copy that panel's contents in the same orientation into blank panels (including across and down), preserving all separator cells. In the test, the top-left 3x6 panel was copied into every other 3x6 panel. The demo used a single vertical color-3 separator; the pattern in the right panel was copied unchanged into the blank left panel.

Practical method: identify separator rows/columns, segment the grid into equal regions, identify source pattern region, then tile/copy its cell arrangement to corresponding blank regions without mirroring. Do not assume reflection: two initial mirror guesses for the test were wrong; exact oriented copying across the compartments was the demonstrated rule.
